headline: Weak Economic Data; Chinese Officials Issue Statement to Calm Markets | Cross-Strait
summary: China's July macroeconomic data was weak. The Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission said the economy should not be judged by individual monthly figures and that its sustained growth trend has not changed.
why: China is the world's second-largest economy, and its macroeconomic data and official signals on growth influence global equities, commodities and currencies.
why_moved: Weak July macroeconomic data prompted an official statement from the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission aimed at calming markets. It stressed that the growth trend has not changed.
